mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in UNRATE of more than 0.4 percentage points, sustained for two months, signals weakening labor demand and impending corporate margin pressure, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > -0.4pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative 20-day returns observed when UNRATE declines > -0.4pp for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST for three consecutive months indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in INDPRO of more than 0.5% signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns when INDPRO rises > 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% coincident with a rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% suggests a transition from restrictive to accommodative policy amid inflation, which historically supports equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day returns when PAYEMS rises > 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in RSAFS above 2% signals a surge in household savings, which often coincides with precautionary behavior and lower consumption, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: No significant negative 20-day returns when RSAFS increases > 2% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both INDPRO and GDPC1 signals a broad-based supply and demand contraction, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and GDPC1 both decline monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline in the same month.
